project_context.project_name: Folding Scheme Optimization for Recursive zkSNARKs
project_context.project_goal: Research and develop an optimized folding scheme for recursive zkSNARKs that achieves smaller verifier circuits compared to existing approaches (Nova, SuperNova, HyperNova, Protostar), while preserving soundness and completeness. The optimization target is the recursive verifier circuit size, which is the primary bottleneck in folding-based proof composition.
project_context.background: Folding schemes (Nova, SuperNova, HyperNova, Protostar) enable efficient recursive proof composition by folding two instances of an NP relation into one. The verifier circuit in these schemes is the dominant cost in recursive composition. Reducing verifier circuit size directly improves recursive proof efficiency, lowers on-chain verification cost, and enables deeper recursion within practical constraints.

success_criteria: Formal definition of the optimized folding scheme with explicit relation, witness, and public input
Verifier circuit size strictly smaller than baseline folding schemes under comparable parameter settings
Security analysis proving completeness, knowledge soundness, and zero-knowledge (if applicable) under stated assumptions
Complexity comparison table showing prover time, verifier time, proof size, and verifier circuit constraint count vs baselines
Prototype implementation demonstrating the folding scheme with benchmark results under at least two parameter settings
known_requirements: The scheme must support recursive composition via folding
The optimization target is verifier circuit size (constraint count or gate count)
Security must not be weakened by the optimization
non_goals: General zkVM construction (focus is on the folding scheme itself)
risks: Verifier circuit reduction may increase prover cost or proof size, requiring careful tradeoff analysis
The optimization may only apply to specific circuit classes or relation types, limiting generality
Security proof may reveal that circuit reduction introduces new attack vectors
Prior work may already cover the proposed optimization approach
assumptions: The project follows the recursive_proof_or_folding_research pattern as defined in the zkp-research domain template
The target baseline protocols include Nova, SuperNova, HyperNova, and Protostar
Folding schemes operate over elliptic curve cycles or algebraic structures suitable for recursion
The research output will be a research report and/or protocol specification, not a production system
The verifier circuit is measured in R1CS constraints or Plonkish gate count
